en: The Sūtra of the Ratnabhadra Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heavens, Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas.
At that time, there was a great yakṣa lord named Ratnabhadra who came to where the Buddha was;
having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet.
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess a Great Secret Heart Dharani which I wish to proclaim.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will look upon me with compassion and grant his protection."
World-Honored One, if there are bhikṣus,
bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who recite and contemplate this dhāraṇī with a sincere mind three times each day, [they shall obtain such benefits].
I shall always act as a source of reliance for those people.
In all matters, they shall attain auspiciousness;
furthermore, I shall constantly provide them with food, drink, clothing, bedding, gold, silver, precious jewels, wealth, grain, and so forth.
Furthermore, it shall cause all benefits to be fully accomplished and ensure that all people universally attain love and respect,
with the sole exception of the evil and unwholesome dharmas such as lust, anger, and delusion.
All other matters he undertook were entirely according to his will.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that this great yakṣa lord Ratnacandra was sincere in his faith and respect,
acted for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings suffering from poverty and affliction.
And he addressed him, saying:
"Excellent, O Great Yakṣa Lord Ratnabhadra!
You are able to bring benefit to all sentient beings."
"I, too, delight to hear you proclaim it as you wish.
Then the great yakṣa lord Ratnabhadra immediately spoke this dhāraṇī.
It is said:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo maṇibhadraya. Mahāyakṣasenāpate.

After the Great Yakṣa Lord Ratnabhadra had spoken this dhāraṇī,
he again addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, if anyone recites this dhāraṇī seven times according to the ritual,
all the benefits they perform will be accomplished.
Furthermore, if there is a person who, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, maintains purity and observes the precepts,
burns aloeswood and sandalwood incense three times each day,
and recites this dhāraṇī eight thousand times in full.
This person, in accordance with their vows, shall obtain gold, silver,
and precious treasures, all as they wish. At that time,
the great yakṣa lord, having spoken this dhāraṇī, prostrated to the Buddha and withdrew.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra,
the assembly of bodhisattvas, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ratnacandra Dhāraṇī.
